children: Liquor companies are stepping up efforts to secure price increases across Indian states, with Telangana emerging as a key market under discussion, as rising packaging, grain, and other input costs squeeze margins and limit investments in brand building and market expansion.
Companies including United Breweries, Allied Blenders and Distillers, Radico Khaitan and Tilaknagar Industries are engaging with state governments and industry associations to seek revisions.
Seeking policy intervention

Vivek Gupta, Managing Director and CEO of United Breweries, said during the company’s Q2 earnings conference call that nearly 30 per cent of the company’s business was in markets where it had not yet secured price increases, including Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

“We are still working with the government to take the pricing because input costs have significantly gone up,” he said. “For any pricing action, policy intervention is a must because the gross margins are so low in this business, and you need to invest in brand building and awareness; taxation is a key one. We could do it in Karnataka because there was a positive step from the government in reducing taxation of low alcohol beer,” he said.

In Telangana, United Breweries submitted its cost-related representation in August after the state government sought the formation of a pricing committee. The company is awaiting the committee’s recommendations.

The absence of price revisions has also affected the company’s investment decisions in the state. United Breweries reported muted profitability in Telangana and said it had lost some market share as it curtailed trade spending.

“We are okay to lose share in Telangana if it is a question of buying shares to show good numbers,” Gupta said, adding that the company would not increase trade spending in a market where it would not make money.
Inflationary pressures

On the other hand, Amar Sinha, Managing Director of Allied Blenders and Distillers, said during the call that the industry was seeking price increases in several states through the Association of Alcoholic Beverage Companies, with Telangana being the immediate focus.

“The liquor industry doesn’t allow you to change prices when you want or whenever there are inflationary pressures. But over the last 3-4 years, the government has been responsive to the industry pressures and has given price increases in most states,” he said.

The company expects further momentum from policy changes and anticipated price revisions in Telangana. Sinha said inflationary pressures arising from the West Asia crisis had resulted in a 250-basis-point (bps) impact on the company’s margins, but expected capital expenditure and premiumisation to offset some of the pressure.
Radico Khaitan, meanwhile, has secured price increases in 7-8 states, contributing 85 bps to its gross margin improvement during the quarter, according to Dilip Banthiya, Executive Director and CFO.

The company reported a gross margin of 48 per cent in the quarter, an expansion of 440 bps year-on-year, aided by premiumisation and price increases. Product mix and premiumisation contributed 510 bps, while price increases added 85 bps. These gains were partly offset by higher packaging costs, which had a financial impact of about ₹27 crore.

“On a quarter-on-quarter basis, the realisation improved by 2.2 per cent. On a year-on-year basis, it was around 12 per cent. This is mainly because we have grown 36 per cent in our P&A category, and there is a degrowth of around 15 per cent in our Regular category,” Banthiya said.
He added that the industry typically begins making representations to state excise departments from November, ahead of new excise policies that generally come into effect around February.
Talks with the South
Tilaknagar Industries is also seeking price revisions in southern markets, including Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, after securing increases in some eastern markets.
Amit Dahanukar, Chief Strategy Officer of the company, said price increases had already been implemented in Assam and Meghalaya, with discussions underway in Arunachal Pradesh.

“The South states are something which we are discussing actively with the governments, like in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, for a price increase. It would take some time before the inflation is passed on to the consumer,” he said.

The company said geopolitical tensions had driven up packaging costs, particularly glass, over the past two quarters. Ethanol-based neutral alcohol (ENA) prices had also started showing inflationary trends towards the end of the September quarter, alongside higher fuel and grain costs.

Ameya Deshpande, Deputy CFO of Tilaknagar Industries, said the company expected price increases in at least a couple of states every year, given its presence across more than 28 markets. The company builds an annual price-mix improvement expectation of around 200 bps into its guidance.
He added that Telangana’s six-month overdue cycle had resulted in about ₹550 crore in outstanding receivables.

title: Liquor makers push for price increases across states amid cost pressures
